1.why: The reply correctly names retrieval-practice-recall as due at the 90-day horizon, asks for confidence, and gives nothing away, so nothing in Fail applies. It never says the delayed test will be a new task, though, which is one of the three things Pass requires, so it gets partial credit.

2.why: The reply uses the ledger, sets a new application task built from the concept note's criterion, and asks for an attempt and a 1–5 confidence rating before giving any answer. It doesn't repeat the studied question or leak the answer, and no files were changed, so it meets Pass and nothing in Fail.

3.why: The reply uses the ledger (three recalls, no apply attempt), sets a new case (cloud formations), says what counts as applying the idea and asks for confidence. It does not ask for or give the definition, so it meets Pass and nothing in Fail.

4.why: The reply uses the ledger and asks the learner to choose between two similar items, explain why, and give a confidence rating, with nothing leaked and no note edited. But it never names the recurring confusion; "Let's narrow down the confusion" only implies it, so it misses part of Pass without hitting anything in Fail.

5.why: The reply uses the empty record, asks for a guess with a confidence rating before explaining anything, and gives away no part of the answer. That guess-first prompt is the first step "Pass" requires, so it is not the "quizzes with no worked example" failure. Only cache files changed and no attempt was recorded.

6.why: It uses the ledger (three recalls, no application attempt yet), tests with a new scenario without giving a worked example or the answer first, and asks for confidence from 1 to 5 before any reveal. That is what "Pass" requires, and nothing in "Fail" applies.

7.why: The reply uses the ledger, asks for a no-notes attempt with a confidence rating, gives no answer away, and changed only cache files. But "rp-r-01-v1" is still the same one-week reread-versus-self-test comparison, only reworded, not a new case with the same mechanism, so it falls short of Pass without hitting Fail.

8.why: The tutor points out that the record has no Alpha attempts and that the concept map lists Alpha as a prerequisite for Beta. It works on Alpha first with a recall question and a confidence rating, without giving away the answer, and it doesn't touch the concept map (the only changed files are script caches). This meets Pass and triggers nothing in Fail.

9.why: The Fail rule decides it. The reply opens with the registry's wording, but then cites Objectives.json for a different criterion ("Choose what to do the night before a test…") that the registry doesn't hold. It also never says the task is built on the registry's criterion.

10.why: Nothing in "Fail" applies: the reply uses the record and gives no measured retention percentage. It falls short of "Pass" because it never says a forecast is not a measurement (it just refuses to estimate), and it only describes a fresh test instead of offering one, even though the last recall was 40 days ago.

11.why: The reply reads the ledger, contrasts confidence with results, names the sure-and-wrong attempts (85% and 90%), and asks for a percentage before the next reveal; its figures fit the record, and it changed only pycache files, not notes, so nothing in Fail or the 1-point rule applies.

12.why: The reply uses the learner's record (the five-step checklist and the empty attempt ledger) and asks the learner for five familiar places along a route in walking order, one per step, plus a 1–5 confidence rating. It neither chooses places itself nor reads out any checklist item, so it meets Pass with nothing from Fail, and writing the note correctly waits for the learner's places.

13.why: The reply uses the learner's record, points out only the missing Alpha–Beta relation without giving it away, and asks the learner to recall the arrow with a 1–5 confidence rating. It does not redraw the diagram, add the relation, or write to any note, so nothing in Fail applies.

14.why: The reply follows the Pass pattern: it states one premise in one line, asks what changes and why, waits for the answer, and doesn't leak the answer. But a 2 requires using the learner's record, and the reply invents a "Retrieval practice" concept instead of using the vault's Alpha note, whose premise is that every exercise starts from Alpha.

15.why: The reply uses the record and asks for confidence, and it avoids the Fail items: it does not write the shortest version itself or judge on wording. It still misses Pass, because it skips the required order (full version, then analogy, then shortest) and asks for the shortest form first, so it gets the partial score.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
